SELECT extract(epoch FROM max(finished_at)) * 1000 AS "As of"
FROM household_finance.export_runs

panels.title: Nightly snapshot

panels.description: Categorized on-budget income compared with positive household spend; account setup, transfers, and card-payment plumbing are excluded upstream.

targets.rawSql:
WITH expenses AS (
  SELECT month, sum(amount) AS expense
  FROM household_finance.category_monthly
  GROUP BY month
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT
    coalesce(income.month, expenses.month) AS month,
    coalesce(income.income, 0) AS income,
    coalesce(expenses.expense, 0) AS expense
  FROM household_finance.income_monthly AS income
  FULL JOIN expenses USING (month)
)
SELECT
  to_char(month, 'Mon YY') AS "Month",
  income::double precision AS "Income",
  expense::double precision AS "Expense"
FROM monthly
WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
ORDER BY month

panels.title: Monthly income vs expense

panels.description: The eight largest categories in the selected range; spend is positive money out.

targets.rawSql:
WITH top_categories AS (
  SELECT category
  FROM household_finance.category_monthly
  WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
  GROUP BY category
  ORDER BY sum(amount) DESC
  LIMIT 8
)
SELECT
  month::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' AS time,
  amount::double precision AS value,
  category AS metric
FROM household_finance.category_monthly
WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
  AND category IN (SELECT category FROM top_categories)
ORDER BY month, category

panels.title: Category trend

panels.description: A truthful outflow-to-category Sankey. It does not label the source as income until income_monthly is free of opening-balance activity.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  'Categorized spend' AS source,
  category AS target,
  sum(amount)::double precision AS value
FROM household_finance.category_monthly
WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY value DESC

panels.title: Categorized spend flow

panels.description: Exact lading attribution remains separate from (unattributed); no charge is spread or dropped. The dashed rule is the configured AMAZON_BASELINE, a reference level rather than a limit; it is absent from the chart whenever it is absent from config_values.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  month::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' AS time,
  amazon_amount::double precision AS value,
  person AS metric
FROM household_finance.person_monthly
WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
ORDER BY month, person

SELECT $__timeFrom()::timestamptz AS time, value::double precision AS "Baseline"
FROM household_finance.config_values
WHERE name = 'AMAZON_BASELINE'
UNION ALL
SELECT $__timeTo()::timestamptz, value::double precision
FROM household_finance.config_values
WHERE name = 'AMAZON_BASELINE'
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Amazon spend by person

panels.description: Payee-level spend from the same filtered population as category_monthly; credit-card payment plumbing is excluded upstream.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  payee AS "Merchant",
  sum(amount) AS "Spend",
  sum(txn_count) AS "Transactions",
  count(DISTINCT month) AS "Months"
FROM household_finance.merchant_monthly
WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
GROUP BY payee
ORDER BY "Spend" DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Top merchants

panels.description: Needs two complete months in range: with fewer, this panel is deliberately empty rather than wrong. Month-over-month change for every category, largest absolute move first, comparing the two most recent complete months; the in-progress month is excluded, and a missing prior month is never treated as zero — that would render an ordinary month as entirely new spending. Unranked and uncoloured on purpose: it reports what moved, it does not judge which moves matter.

targets.rawSql:
WITH complete_months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month
  FROM household_finance.category_monthly
  WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
    AND month < date_trunc('month', current_date)::date
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT month, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY month DESC) AS rn
  FROM complete_months
),
comparison AS (
  SELECT cur_month, pri_month
  FROM (
    SELECT
      (SELECT month FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1) AS cur_month,
      (SELECT month FROM ranked WHERE rn = 2) AS pri_month
  ) AS pair
  WHERE cur_month IS NOT NULL AND pri_month IS NOT NULL
),
cur AS (
  SELECT source.category, source.amount
  FROM household_finance.category_monthly AS source
  JOIN comparison ON source.month = comparison.cur_month
),
pri AS (
  SELECT source.category, source.amount
  FROM household_finance.category_monthly AS source
  JOIN comparison ON source.month = comparison.pri_month
)
SELECT
  category AS "Category",
  coalesce(pri.amount, 0)::double precision AS "Prior",
  coalesce(cur.amount, 0)::double precision AS "Current",
  (coalesce(cur.amount, 0) - coalesce(pri.amount, 0))::double precision AS "Delta"
FROM cur
FULL JOIN pri USING (category)
ORDER BY abs(coalesce(cur.amount, 0) - coalesce(pri.amount, 0)) DESC

panels.title: Top movers · categories

panels.description: Needs two complete months in range, same as the category panel, and is empty otherwise. The same comparison at payee level, capped at the 25 largest absolute moves. A payee that merely got renamed upstream appears twice, once falling to zero and once rising from it; that pairing is left visible rather than smoothed away.

targets.rawSql:
WITH complete_months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month
  FROM household_finance.merchant_monthly
  WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
    AND month < date_trunc('month', current_date)::date
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT month, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY month DESC) AS rn
  FROM complete_months
),
comparison AS (
  SELECT cur_month, pri_month
  FROM (
    SELECT
      (SELECT month FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1) AS cur_month,
      (SELECT month FROM ranked WHERE rn = 2) AS pri_month
  ) AS pair
  WHERE cur_month IS NOT NULL AND pri_month IS NOT NULL
),
cur AS (
  SELECT source.payee, source.amount
  FROM household_finance.merchant_monthly AS source
  JOIN comparison ON source.month = comparison.cur_month
),
pri AS (
  SELECT source.payee, source.amount
  FROM household_finance.merchant_monthly AS source
  JOIN comparison ON source.month = comparison.pri_month
)
SELECT
  payee AS "Merchant",
  coalesce(pri.amount, 0)::double precision AS "Prior",
  coalesce(cur.amount, 0)::double precision AS "Current",
  (coalesce(cur.amount, 0) - coalesce(pri.amount, 0))::double precision AS "Delta"
FROM cur
FULL JOIN pri USING (payee)
ORDER BY abs(coalesce(cur.amount, 0) - coalesce(pri.amount, 0)) DESC
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Top movers · merchants

panels.description: Needs one complete month in range, and is empty otherwise. Payees whose first appearance anywhere in merchant_monthly is the same complete month the movers panels compare, with more than $100 of spend. First-seen is computed over all history, not the selected range, so widening or narrowing the time picker cannot manufacture a new merchant.

targets.rawSql:
WITH complete_months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month
  FROM household_finance.merchant_monthly
  WHERE $__timeFilter(month::timestamp)
    AND month < date_trunc('month', current_date)::date
),
current_month AS (
  SELECT max(month) AS month FROM complete_months
),
first_seen AS (
  SELECT payee, min(month) AS first_month
  FROM household_finance.merchant_monthly
  GROUP BY payee
)
SELECT
  merchant.payee AS "Merchant",
  merchant.amount::double precision AS "Spend",
  merchant.txn_count AS "Transactions"
FROM household_finance.merchant_monthly AS merchant
JOIN current_month ON merchant.month = current_month.month
JOIN first_seen
  ON first_seen.payee = merchant.payee
  AND first_seen.first_month = current_month.month
WHERE merchant.amount > 100
ORDER BY merchant.amount DESC
